issues.legal_issue: A release application based on personal need is outside the purchase-related waiting-period bar when it is filed more than three years after execution of a registered transfer, because the transfer operates from its execution date.
material_facts: The landlord sought release of the premises on the ground of personal need.
The sale deed was executed before it was offered and admitted for registration; its later transcription into the registration records did not alter the date from which it operated.
The release application was filed more than three years after execution of the deed.
issues.conclusion: The application was filed after the three-year period had elapsed, so the proviso was not attracted. The appeal was dismissed. The Court did not need to decide whether the proviso bars entertaining an application during the three-year period or only bars making an eviction order during that period.
issues.legal_principle: The first proviso to Section 21(1) of the U.P. Urban Building (Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972 restricts a personal-need release application during the prescribed period after purchase. Under Section 47 of the Indian Registration Act, 1908, once a deed is registered, it operates from the time it would have operated had registration not been required; here, that was the date of execution, not the later date when it was transcribed into the registration record. No earlier cases were relied on.

predicates.personal_need_release_application: A landlord applies for release of rented premises on the ground of personal need.
predicates.transfer_deed_executed_and_registered: The landlord executes a deed transferring the premises, and the deed is subsequently registered.
predicates.application_filed_more_than_three_years_: The landlord files the release application more than three years after executing the deed.

issues.definition: When a landlord files a personal-need release application more than three years after executing a deed that is subsequently registered, the purchase-related waiting-period bar does not apply.
